details:
Issue:
When designing multiple worlds meant for navigation, IE an exploration based network of worlds that encourages groups of players to 'roam' between worlds, naturally exploring, it is currently extremely unreliable to expect players who all go through the same portal to actually end up in the same instance on the other end.
To compensate for this, world designers often opt to build larger monolithic worlds. This has negative consequences for the servers and players. If a player were to visit a world and only explore one quarter of it, they had to load and store 75% of the world unnecessarily, and the server had to consume those resources and bandwidth as well.
Proposal:
Some form of options on the portal object to be a new instance when spawned, inheriting the same privacy settings as the instance the portal was spawned in.
Effectively, when this is specified, upon the new instance containing the portals is generated, each of the portals also bind to a new instance. However, that of course would likely have disastrous effects, since you can create an infinite loop by just linking two worlds in a feedback loop together.
To solve this, two things probably are best to handle this.
1. The portal will lazy bind, only actually generating its instance the first time a user enters it
2. Portals should have some logic to detect if the world id they point to is the same as the world Id they were generated from. So if World A has a portal to World B, and World B has a portal to A, if I Go from A to B via instance generation, the B>A portal should use the instance it "came from" rather than generating a new one.
The intended effect here would be such that if a user hops through a portal to a new instance, then returns back via a "return" portal that world happens to have setup, they can semi reliably expect to end up back in the instance they came from with their friends again.
(Caveats of course for if this would involve them trying to join an already full instance, in which case it would overflow them to a new instance as a fallthrough)

If there is an intention specifically to encourage meeting of strangers behind the current design, then there is potentially one more caveat to add to the portal's instance selection, and that would be a "Fit First" sorting to instance selection.

This would effectively prioritize, rather than spinning up a new instance, instead selecting a "everyone can fit" instance if possible. For example, if World A has 8 users in it and a portal to World B, which has a max capacity of 24 users, the portal would first attempt to find a currently existing instance that *also* has room for all 8 users to fit into, and prioritize that zone first.

Reason:
A fair number of world builders, myself included, are really seeming to dig more into the artistic and design style of building individual worlds that cohesively "glue" together to encourage and reward players for taking portals and exploring, which I believe is a core design philosophy of the VRC team.
However, player's suspension of disbelief and engagement becomes interrupted often when they attempt to travel between worlds and often find their group of friends becomes broken up and scattered across different instances.
This "downside" encourages world designers to instead opt into more monolithic, larger style worlds that manually handle exploration/trave/teleportation within the world itself.
Unfortunately, these large monolithic worlds are quite the burden, if not incompatible, with quest users, which appears to be an important demographic for the VRC team.
In order to encourage world designers to "break up" their worlds into managable sizes (which lowers hardware requirements and encourages lazy loading of unused assets not explored), it is imperative a more cohesive logic be baked into how portals between worlds works.
Summary
If we make portals less random feeling and more consistent between worlds, it will encourage world makers to make more smaller worlds, rather than unified monolithic worlds, which is better for Quest users for sure, and probably just better for server health/bandwidth overall.
title: Add support for "New Instance" synched to first enter on Portals
